Signalis has great worldbuilding, and extremely interesting visuals. It wears its influences on its sleeve a bit too hard, but what is unique about it is excellent and it uses what it borrows masterfully; so I'd never criticize it for it.

The community that spread around this game is completely deranged (positive).

Want to know if this game is worth your money? Here are the pros and cons:

PROS:
- Great graphics and art direction in the vein of classic survival horror games
- Good story that keeps you roped in
- Easy gameplay that offers lots of ways to play
- Great atmosphere
- Great enemy variety
- Great sound design
- Halo 3 Believe soundtrack
- Good story length
- Cheap price

CONS:
- Story is a little hard to understand at times (But it's meant to be that way - Watch some fan theories after you play)
- Some text in cutscenes are not translated from game dev's native languages
- Some puzzles are not explained very well. Had to Google a few times
- Elster is not currently stepping on me

When Signalis 2? Need more peg-legged space mommy.
Signalis has been living rent free in my head since I touched it. How absolutely devastating, beautiful, perfect, this game is, holy shit.
awesome game with very creepy atmosphere. there was a bunch of german i wasn't able to understand, but that didnt take away from the story of the game that much.
A love letter to classic horror gamed like Resident Evil and Silent Hill that nonetheless stands up on its own! 10/10!

Signalis is one of the best survival horror games I've played in recent years. The story, artstyle, sound and gameplay is all absolutely stellar. The game takes inspiration from the classics like Silent Hill and Resident Evil, applying the best lessons from those games while also adding its own unique twists. If you're a fan of survival horror games you owe it to yourself to give this a shot.

I dont review games but this one is so special. Ive never played a game that made me feel so seen yet so alone at the same time. As someone who doesnt play psychological horror games there were times during this game where i felt like it was hard to continue forward out of fear of what was next. Theres just something about this game that draws me in and is keeping me in, It makes me feel like im missing something that I used to have so close to me, and something ill never get back no matter how much I yearn and beg for it to return. Its such a soul crushing feeling that makes me crave this game even more, even if I cried so hard enough at the end that I thought I was going to be sick to my stomach and couldnt talk about it for 48 hours without tearing up. Its such a painfully beautiful experience and I believe it genuinely changed my life however I cant say if it was for better or for worse. My heart aches and I cant get it out of my head.

(With a bonus of a gorgeous soundtrack <3)

For my first foray into the survival horror genre, I cannot reccomend this game enough. A well done story, nerve wracking gameplay, and outstanding enviornmental design. I cannot reccomend it enough to anyone looking to try a survival horror game. 10/10. I am already anticipating the next time I play it.

Signalis probably has become one of my favorite horror anything in general. Signalis tells the tale of holding onto connection and love in the midst of a collapsing world that refuses to be understood...and that's all I can say about it without giving any spoilers. I understand that the way the tale is told is not for everyone, but the gameplay and art would definitely satisfy you. With its classic survival horror a la resident evil and silent hill albeit with a top down approach and the stellar pixelated environment that I would say is up there with the most atmospheric games I've ever played. Not to mention its anime drawn characters that makes the art direction unique and amazing. A little PSA before playing tho, the game has a fake ending, so look out for that (I'm saying this because I've seen some people thought that the fake ending is the actual ending).
SUPER! Ich liebe SIGNALIS! Amazing game, have not finished, plan on doing so soon. Gameplay is amazing, story is mildly confusing.
Its simply one of the best survival horror experiences ever. I have no notes. Play it if you love classic survival horror, enjoy.

There is so much to praise here!

The blend of isometric survival horror gameplay, from time to time interrupted by 3D puzzle and exploration, topped off with gorgeous pixel art cutscenes results in an amazing experience. Puzzles are just right. Inventory management raises the difficulty of the game in a different way.

And I didn't even mention the content yet! The story is so intriguing. Each time a cutscene starts, there is so much happening! It's distracting, confusing, but well done enough to make you curious about what happens next. Uncovering the story piece by piece. The mysterious atmoshpere is so strong. Even just exploring the corridors can be terrifying, especially if you're running low on supplies. It's a beautiful and complex story, it might be worth another playthrough to understand it better.

The music is amazing and the sound design is solid.

I love this game. Greatly recommend!

This is the best survival horror I've ever played, and my all-time favourite horror game. It wears its influences on its sleeve and that doesn't detract from the experience at all. The story is as emotionally destructive as it is confusing, and I'm infinitely happy to have found this game.

Please purchase and enjoy it, as that's the best way to experience all it has to offer.

All I ask from a survival horror game is to make me feel paranoid and not just actually make me feel like I'm surviving something or someone, but making my progression worth the journey and its conclusion. Signalis did all of that and made me feel a cacophony of feelings, the prime one being many many tears coming to the end of my survival with one of the many endings. What drives me with these kinds of games is that feeling of survival. Feeling like you're scraping by with the bare minimum to defend yourself against whatever threat or threats are present. This feeling alone could bring me through a game I normally wouldn't bring myself to continue playing. I can confidently say I myself never found a boring moment in this game as there was always an enemy to put down, a relatively simple puzzle to solve, and an overall objective to pursue, all in the name of survival and purpose. I can't get into the rest of what this game offers without writing an entire thesis so to anyone whose interest is even remotely peaked from what you've seen, give it a shot. In the end, everyone's tastes are different. I just hope that you can experience what myself and many others who recommend this game now most likely have as rent free memories.

KICK EM WHILE THEY'RE DOWN

Randomly remembered I didn't put a review in for this game. Suffice to say, it's amazing even remembering it years later. Jesus fucking christ this game destroyed me. And I don't even mean the puzzles, though some of them are insane. One of those games where you have to sit in silence and stare at a wall afterwards, play it NOW

Signalis is a psychological horror game that raises a lot of questions at the start, but in the end all the pieces slowly fall together as you go through your journey. It's dark, atmospheric, and makes you question your very journey throughout. It's a trip and it's a trip I will happily go through again. It's a rare a game can make me ugly cry by the end with an ending that not only breaks your heart, but your soul hurts as well. 10/10 this is what modern survival horror should be.

I've played this game through about three times now and it has been one of the best puzzle/survival horror game experiences I've had in a long while!! The story leaves you wanting more, searching for answers in everything you find, your second or third play through will have you understanding and realising a lot of things that you might not have in your first. The game play is also extremely enjoyable and I find myself trying to find reasons to replay it just so I can experience it again. Fantastic game, worth every penny and every second spent playing.

A game with an incredible story, incredible characters, and an incredible world. 10/10. 100% would recommend to anyone who likes psychological horror.

It is impossible to explain what is so gripping and ultimately beautiful about this game without giving spoilers. So, I will avoid spoiling anything and simply make comparisons.

The world and general vibe feels like Dead Space mixed with Nier Automata. Mechanically, playing the game feels like Metal Gear Solid crossed with Resident Evil with escape room puzzles straight out of the Zero Escape series. It also features insightful consideration of various science fiction concepts you are probably familiar with, but have likely not seen explored in exactly this same way. It also does so with stylish retro flair that brought me back to the feeling of playing games on my Playstation as a kid. Expect to experience truly crushing despair and hopelessness, but also eureka moments and genuine triumph. 

Hitting the credits does not take very long, but it really doesn't see the full scope of what this game has to offer. I cannot stress enough that you SHOULD jump back in even after playing through the first time. I am writing this before I go back for thirds with a specific idea of stuff I want to try out. Do yourself a favor and play the game blind. Experience this dark, artistic, intense, sci fi horror epic all alone (preferably in a dark room). It is absolutely worth taking your time for this one...

Wake up.

Damn, what a powerful ending. This is one of those games where you play it again after having put it all together and you see everything different because you know what's up now. And even that is taken into consideration with your replay being thematically consistent! That's crazy. They built a story where playing again is an extension of the original playthrough.
Visuals are awesome. Sound is awesome. Gameplay is treading that fine survival horror line between "I have all the bullets", and "please stop ganging up on me robot overlords".
If I have to detract, there's not really many bosses - only three (one for each act), and a room filled with standard enemies is more dangerous than any of the bosses. Challenge is limited, but figuring out the mystery of the story is the focus, and the worldbuilding really was great.

Definite recommend for any sci-fi or survival horror fan.

One of the best game released this year. Definitely worth playing.

Sci-fi cyberpunk with anime girls.

Well-developed storylines and lore interconnected with gameplay, allowing players to discover all the hidden details and learn about characters and the world's history.

Play it if you really, really liked Silent Hill 1 or 2, you'll love this, probably.

Personally, I wasn't much a fan for the actual main story, but I came into this game expecting something different than what I got. However, the pixel art and passion for the game is just so, so good.

One of the sections almost made me quit and downvote the game though. If you played it, you probably know which one. That entire section could be removed and almost nothing would be lost. Arguably I've heard some theories of what that area is, but I still dislike it for several reasons. The gameplay was a massive cliff of difficulty as the first, but that wasn't the biggest reason. It robbed Signalis of its voice for a time by pulling reference too hard. It stopped being Signalis to use Silent Hill's style to convey similar information to Silent Hill's story. But I wanted more Signalis, not Silent Hill. The sudden rise in tedious monster gameplay just helped make the area feel more hollow and less like Signalis as a result.

But that was the only part of the game that really hurt my enjoyment and it was ultimately a small part.

This is a must have for Resident Evil and Silent Hill fans, as it brings back the best of the survival horror genre, while adding cyberpunk existentialism to the mix.

Signalis captures the strangeness of reality.

The pursuing of a goal, a goal given to you by someone else.
The self actualization achieved along the way of pursuing that goal.
The betrayal of realizing once its too late, that goal is the opposite of what you wanted.
The hopelessness of realizing its all too late to change.

However these developers came up with this medium as a way to tell this story is beyond me.
This is a masterpiece of art, unlike anything else.

Is Signalis a masterpiece? Yes.
Does rose-engine deserve all the praise and accolades for creating this game? Absolutely yes.
Is Signalis just a good game in general? Also yes.

Is Signalis a PERFECT game? No, unfortunately.

While I do easily recommend this game to everyone, this game can be HARD. It's modelled after old-school survival horror, where resources are scarce and it's often better to flee then fight. This can lead to some frustrating scenarios, where it feels like your in a death-respawn loop, and have to brute force your way forward. The developers have made the game "easier" by default, but it can still be a tricky time. Despite all that though, the story is beautiful and the game play is solid. This game is worth your time.

Once again, this is a 10/10 game. It might be difficult to get into, but it is worth the time and effort that you put in.

The main thing about Signalis it's being an homage to old survival horror, but it also adds alot of new things. Do not play it expecting jump scares or a lot of action, it's more of an atmospheric slow burn, with a very cryptic story, but still manages to have interesting characters. The puzzles are not that hard so dont use a guide in your first playthrough it will kill all the magic of the game.

Unironically absolute cinema. The story is phenomenal, every cutscene is chilling and the worldbuilding is done very similarly to resident evil.

Tense combat that actually forces you to consider if fighting is even worth it; resource and inventory management that actually make you feel like you're struggling, the difficulty is done very well. There is nothing for you here.

I could not sing the art direction's praises any harder if i tried. The music is incredible, the visuals are incredible, the aesthetics are incredible. I struggle to describe this game to people succinctly because it is that good. They cooked so hard, and mind you that rose engine is 2 people. Why are you still here anyway? Buy it.

I finished up one run of this last week (with one ending) and it took me a while to process my thoughts.

In order to understand the narrative, you probably need to watch a lot of the analysis videos. I don't think I'm prepared to do that. The storytelling is, in some ways, a little too abstract; I think I prefer this a bit more in novels like "House of Leaves" or something by Samuel Beckett where that technique is handled better.

The gameplay reminds me of old horror survival titles with a very limited inventory and a lot of backtracking/item management. That kind of pads the game's length out a bit too much in my opinion. Enemies that keep reviving become a bit annoying in places, but it's OKAY overall. 

The puzzles can be genuinely confusing, and I'd lying if I said I didn't look up hints from time to time on how to solve them.

I'd say what saves this game for me is its overall atmosphere. It just absolutely nails this aspect and you can't help but keep playing it for the creepy vibes even though you have no idea what's going on most of the time. It's almost good enough in this one category alone to make me overlook the pacing/inventory issues.

I still kind of wish they had attempted to write a slightly more coherent story, but it's still very much worth playing at least once.

Great game, excellent visuals with a well done tense horror atmosphere. I thought item placement was fair, items are scarce enough that the choice to use them feels just like that, a choice. There was only one time where I was struggling for meds or ammo (I believe I was playing on the medium difficulty). The light puzzles involved are a nice addition and are something refreshing after going through a corridor of terror. The only real downside I kinda abused later on was going through doors to avoid combat. This kinda killed tension for me as I would just sprint past enemies, whereas before I often walked much more and avoided or strategically eliminated certain enemies. Overall though, I would highly recommend playing.

The sounds are super powerful in this game from the menu to in game, and then the changes from 3rd person to 1st person is so well done, the scenery is perfect as well, and the puzzles fit into the game perfectly cause a lot of games have puzzles but they feel very out of place but signalis puts puzzles in the game very well.

This game is incredibly fun. The experience of seeing everything and collecting each little note to piece together the story is really great. Bit by bit you feel like you're understanding things, but as you get more pieces some things don't fit with whatever you were piecing together and you have to try and connect things in a different way. The gameplay of weighing what enemies you can sneak by against how much ammunition you have and what healing resources you have if things go wrong is really engaging. I think Signalis is best without any previous exposure to it's story and characters. It 100% deserves it's Overwhelmingly Positive review percentage.

Very few stories have made me cry from pulling my heartstrings to the point of outright breaking them. So far it's been Signalis, Void Stranger, Madoka Magica, and Land of the Lustrous.

If I played this in 2022, it likely would've been my game of the year.

Signalis is a game with a story that may be difficult to follow and incredible gameplay to experience it through. The inventory was a bit of a concern at first, but once I adapted to how the game flows, I got confident enough to travel lighter and lighter still and my inventory became a non issue. I haven't played enough horror games to properly articulate how well Signalis' horror works, all I can really say is that the atmosphere is on point and the artstyle is immaculate. I absolutely adore a game that takes 3D assets and makes them convincingly appear 2D, Guilty Gear emulated hand drawn animation and now Signalis emulates isometric backgrounds.

If I have to point out some criticisms towards the game, you take damage from touching enemies and, though rare, it is possible to be forced to walk into one when entering a room before you're able to act. More often than not, you only get dangerously close and can just shove them away, but once in a while you will get unlucky and take unfair damage. Regardless of how rare it is, it is still a problem that it can happen at all.

I don't have much else to say, so I'm just gonna end it here and listen to "The Promise" on loop for an hour, have a nice day.

I accidentally found SIGNALIS while scrolling through the Steam discovery queue, and it has to be simultaneously the best accidental find I've ever made and the most heart-wrenching experience playing a game in recent memory. I've never played any of the old horror games that had a massive influence on this game, Resident Evil and Silent Hill, chief amongst them. The art style and premise hooked me first, with the story, universe, and background events getting me with the sinker. If you enjoy an emotionally charged story that respects your ability to put the pieces together, with amazing background lore, I can't recommend it enough. Just remember to keep (Y)our Promise.

Signalis is one of those cases where I recognize that it's a good game in a style that doesn't really do much for me these days. It's a really good take on the old Alone in the Dark/early Resident Evil style survival horror games; limited inventory capacity, limited resources, a mix of item and knowledge-based puzzles, avoidance of enemies as a valid strategy, etc. The aesthetics are really cool, it's doing some funky things with the storytelling, and the enemies being various forms of sci-fi biomechanical horrors was neat. 

That said, I've just generally worked through my interest in that style of horror game though, and while I was fine with seeing this through, it didn't wow me like it did a lot of folks, and I'm aware that's a me issue, not anything Signalis did wrong. I do recommend it if you like the retro-styled survival horror genre and somehow haven't gotten around to it.

Signalis truly left an impression on me, but not because it revealed to me something I've lived without for so long, rather, I'd say my experience with it validated my tale of life and hardship. Even for a first playthrough, its symbolism wasn't lost on me, especially when I saw that it directly used my favorite painting ever made. Once I saw it, everything fell into place, and I knew exactly what the story wanted to tell us. Perhaps a very different experience for most people, but regardless, Signalis has the ability to truly touch your heart, and I wouldn't give it up for anything in the world.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (97%): players love the story and characters, which 59% of reviews praise.
The main complaints are the story and the gameplay, though few reviews raise either.

details.text: Complaints about the story have eased lately: 5% of recent reviews raise them, down from 8% overall.
Early players are less positive, at 80% positive, while long-time players are far more upbeat.
